transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Verdant InfoSec), Priya Rao (CTO), Liam O'Neill (Procurement), Nadia Gomez (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Verdant's vendor risk questionnaire (combined SIG + custom form). Focus on encryption/KMS options, audit logging / retention, RBAC/SSO, and data residency for certain PHI-related workloads. Agreed to exchange redacted SOC 2 and SIG snapshot and schedule a deeper technical runbook session.

Topics covered: SOC 2 evidence, SIG mappings, CAIQ references, private deployment (VPC), KMS options, audit log exports, SSO (SAML), role scoping, data residency controls.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex: Alex here.
[00:07] Priya: Priya on from Verdant.
[00:09] Liam: Liam, procurement.
[00:11] Nadia: Nadia, compliance.
[00:12] Sofia: Great. Marcus and Jordan from our side as well. We'll walk through the SIG and your form, call out typical evidence, and then leave time for any architecture questions.
[00:25] Marcus: Yep I'll pick up on the technical controls, especially around key management and logging.
[00:30] Liam: To be clear for procurement, the ask is the usual — SOC 2 Type II, encryption, and how we can get attestations for data residency.
[00:37] Sofia: Totally, good to surface that early. Alex, do you want to outline the highest friction items from your intake form?
[00:43] Alex: Sure, the big ones for us: 1) Where keys live and who rotates them; 2) Does the vendor have access to plaintext; 3) Audit logs and how long they're retained; 4) Can we guarantee EU-only residency for some datasets.
[00:59] Marcus: On keys, Redwood supports multiple options — hosted managed keys, customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, and for dedicated/private we can integrate with an HSM. In practice for PHI customers we recommend CMKs in the customer's AWS account so you control rotation and access.
[01:18] Priya: When you say "integrate with HSM", is that on our side or do you host a cluster that connects to our HSM?
[01:25] Marcus: Good question. For Private deployments we can either deploy inside your VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM endpoints, or for Dedicated we can set up a cross-account KMS key policy. There's a bit of setup either way, but the net result is that Redwood never holds the unencrypted customer key material.
[01:41] Nadia: And what about audit logs? We need im tamper-evident logs and retention for 7 years in our policy.
[01:49] Jordan: We provide structured audit logs with timestamps, request metadata, model id, route, token counts, and user id (if passed). Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via S3, CloudWatch, or syslog. For tamper evidence, we support write-once S3 buckets plus CloudTrail integration — we can outline the end-to-end pattern.
[02:09] Alex: Do those logs include prompt text by default?
[02:12] Marcus: By default we include full request/response payloads in logs for debugging, but we can configure redaction at the ingestion point. For regulated workloads we usually recommend tokenization or hashing of PHI prior to storage, or to use request-side data masking.
[02:26] Priya: If we mask at the client, we'd still want to traceability to correlate requests to sessions — is that supported?
[02:33] Jordan: Yes, we have correlation IDs you can pass, and we keep the mapping metadata separate from the payload. That way you can retain traceability without storing raw PHI.
[02:42] Liam: On the SIG itself — there's a question about shared responsibility for penetration testing evidence. Can you summarize what you provide?
[02:49] Sofia: Sure, Redwood provides our internal penetration test reports and a summary of our external vendor assessments. We can provide redacted reports for SOC 2 and pentest findings, and we maintain a list of third-party subprocessors. Very often customers ask for screenshots or configuration evidence — we can supply console screenshots for things like IAM policies and VPC peering configs as part of the evidence bundle.
[03:11] Alex: For SOC 2, do you have a current Type II report?
[03:14] Sofia: We do. We'll share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and the SOC bridge letter.
[03:19] Nadia: We'll need the scope statement — which systems and regions are in scope.
[03:23] Sofia: Yes, scope info included in that package.
[03:26] Priya: Data residency — can you pin data to a specific region for the hosted product?
[03:32] Marcus: For our hosted offering we can pin to a region for storage and compute in many cases; for strict residency we advise Private deployment inside the customer's VPC. There are latency and cost tradeoffs, obviously.
[03:44] Alex: Also, question about RBAC — our security team wants fine-grained role scoping and audit trail of admin actions.
[03:51] Jordan: We support RBAC with role definitions for admin, operator, reader, and can integrate with SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning for groups. All admin actions are logged and are queryable via the audit logs.
[04:05] Priya: Do you support SCIM delta sync with our identity provider?
[04:08] Marcus: Yep, full SCIM provisioning available for our enterprise customers. You can push groups and users and map to roles.
[04:15] Liam: One of the procurement items — indemnity and data breach timelines. Can you confirm your incident notification SLA?
[04:21] Sofia: We commit to 72-hour notification for incidents affecting confidentiality, and we have an incident response runbook we can share. For enterprise contracts we can discuss tighter SLAs.
[04:32] Alex: For evidence, would you be able to provide a sample of the audit log showing a delete event and associated metadata? We want to test retention / deletion claims.
[04:41] Jordan: We can produce a redacted sample. It will include event id, timestamp, actor id, action, resource id, and a hash of the payload — we can redact the payload itself.
[04:51] Nadia: Do you permit on-premises deployment (air-gapped)? We have a couple of clinical systems that require that.
[04:57] Marcus: We do have an on-prem option. It's heavier lift; we'd need to scope network, hardware, and an offline installation checklist. We also support a VPC-only Private deployment that is not air-gapped but keeps all customer data in your cloud account.
[05:12] Priya: For encryption at rest, is everything encrypted using AES-256?
[05:16] Marcus: Yes AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. With customer-managed keys, you control rotation and deletion — Redwood uses KMS Envelope encryption patterns.
[05:25] Alex: There's a SIG row about logical separation between customer workloads — are noisy neighbor risks mitigated?
[05:30] Jordan: With Dedicated and Private we offer tenant isolation at the pod and node level. We run hardware pinning for Dedicated GPU pools and network isolation for Private. For hosted multi-tenant we have resource cgroups and per-request namespace isolation — we can send the performance isolation doc.
[05:46] Sofia: Ok let's talk about timelines — procurement wants to close by end of October. Is that realistic if we can get the evidence bundle?
[05:55] Liam: If we get the SOC and the SIG snapshot this week, we can move quickly. We still need legal review but that timeline is possible.
[06:02] Sofia: Great, we'll get the SOC and SIG snapshot to you by Wednesday. Marcus, anything else on technical blockers?
[06:09] Marcus: Just to note — for EU residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in eu-west region; for low-latency EU serving, dedicated capacity is usually the best tradeoff. Also, if you need HSM-backed keys, that adds lead time for provisioning.
[06:25] Priya: How long is the lead time for HSM?
[06:27] Marcus: Depends on the partner and shape, but plan for 2-4 weeks for final setup and key exchange in typical cases. Could be shorter with pre-approved templates.
[06:36] Alex: One more — do you have a documented deletion/ERASURE procedure? We need a playbook to include in our assessment.
[06:44] Jordan: Yes, we have a delete-by-id API and a retention manager. We'll include the deletion playbook in the evidence package. It shows steps for logical deletion, data purge, and KMS key rotation for crypto-erase scenarios.
[06:59] Sofia: Ok perfect. If there are no more q's, we'll recap next steps.
[07:03] Priya: That's it from me.
[07:05] Alex: All clear.
[07:06] Liam: Thanks.
[07:07] Nadia: Thanks all.

Recap / Close:
- Redwood to share redacted SOC 2 Type II, SOC bridge letter, SIG snapshot and an evidence checklist (S3 link).
- SE will provide architecture diagrams for VPC/private deployment, KMS integration notes, and a sample redacted audit log.
- Verdant to highlight highest-risk SIG rows and share timeline constraints.
- Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with infra/security for week of 2026-10-12.

End of transcript.
